challenges.title: Book Shelf Challenge
challenges.description: Arrange 24 science books and 18 math books on shelves so each shelf has the same number of each type, with no books left over. What is the greatest number of shelves you can use?
descriptionLines: Arrange 24 science books and 18 math books on shelves so each shelf has the same number of each type,
with no books left over. What is the greatest number of shelves you can use?
challenges.successMessage: Correct! Each shelf has 4 Science and 3 Math books.

solution.title: Solution
steps: To find the greatest number of shelves, we need to find the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of 24 and 18.
Each shelf will have 4 Science books and 3 Math books

challenges.title: Cookie Gift Box Challenge
challenges.description: Pack 36 Chocolate cookies and 48 Vanilla cookies into gift boxes so each box has the same number of each flavour, with no cookies leftover. What is the greatest number of gift boxes you can use?
descriptionLines: Pack 36 Chocolate cookies and 48 Vanilla cookies into gift boxes so each box has the same number of each flavour,
with no cookies leftover. What is the greatest number of gift boxes you can use?
challenges.successMessage: ✅ Perfect! Each gift box has 3 Chocolate and 4 Vanilla cookies.

solution.title: Solution
steps: To find the maximum number of gift boxes, we need to find the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of 36 and 48.
Each gift box will have 3 Chocolate cookies and 4 Vanilla cookies

challenges.title: Flower Bouquet Challenge
challenges.description: Arrange 45 Roses and 30 Tulips into identical bouquets so each bouquet has the same number of each flower type, with no leftover flowers. What is the greatest number of bouquets you can make?
descriptionLines: Arrange 45 Roses and 30 Tulips into identical bouquets so each bouquet has the same number of each flower type,
with no leftover flowers. What is the greatest number of bouquets you can make?
challenges.successMessage: ✅ Beautiful! Each bouquet has 4 Roses and 3 Tulips.

solution.title: Solution
steps: To find the maximum number of identical bouquets, we need to find the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of 45 and 30.
Each bouquet will have 3 Roses and 2 Tulips
